title: བསྟན་འགྱུར། སྡེ་དགེ། དབུ་མ། ཤ (Derge Tengyur, vol. 106)
shelf_note: Derge woodblock folio of a Madhyamaka commentary (on the applications of mindfulness and the two truths, glossing a root text in the Bodhicaryāvatāra IX style); belongs in the dbu ma section of the Tengyur.
structure_note: The facsimile's printed margin page number reads '302' while the record is page 301; this is an ordinary offset between the reprint's pagination and the scan index, not a defect seen on this page.

tr_errors_A.english: (absent: the quotation begins at "If one does not see that which is to be felt...")
tr_errors_A.problem: First line of the Dharmasaṃgīti verse ('Feeling is called experience') silently dropped

tr_errors_A.english: that too is established other <note>than it</note>, namely by the intellect of another mental continuum
tr_errors_A.problem: གཞན་ཏེ glosses 'by another' (i.e. another continuum); 'established other than it' is garbled, though the following clause recovers the sense; also 'posited' rendered 'established'

tr_errors_A.english: Wishing simultaneously to teach the application of mindfulness to phenomena as the justification for that very point
tr_errors_A.problem: Two things taught together (the reasoning for that point, and the mindfulness of phenomena) collapsed into one, making the mindfulness the justification

tr_errors_B.english: By what can the self experience anything?
tr_errors_B.problem: 'the self' is read into ཉིད; the verse asks who/what experiences what, with no self introduced

tr_errors_B.english: Apart from a deep-seated attachment to feelings, sensation
tr_errors_B.problem: 'to feelings' supplied; the object of the fixation is on the previous page ('…as X'), not feelings

pages.prefer_reason: Neither has a serious error, but A drops the opening line of the quoted verse and garbles 'by another', while B renders the whole page with only minor over-readings.

book_verdict: A correct Derge Madhyamaka folio with a clean transcription; both English versions are faithful in substance, B slightly more complete (A drops one verse line).
